clue.text: After a ballot, ring a very handsome young man

indicators.note: after tells us the ring comes behind the ballot pieces in the build

parts.note: taken as written
a poll is a vote or ballot
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone wins a vote and then telephones a gorgeous young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Apollo was the Greek god whose name became shorthand for male beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a handsome youth an Apollo is a standard figurative use of the god's name.

clue.text: French composer almost bitten by boy's dog

indicators.note: something bitten is held in the jaws, so the shortened composer sits inside the boy

parts.note: a boy's name; the 's is just part of the surface

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Erik Satie, French composer of the Gymnopédies

explanation.surface: A boy's dog has taken a bite out of a visiting French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer is Erik Satie, known for the Gymnopédies; 'boy's' looks possessive but just supplies a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian is the British name for the German shepherd breed of dog.

clue.text: One may be studied by a lepidopterist operating abroad

definitions.text: One may be studied by a lepidopterist

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A butterfly expert doing field work overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating abroad' reads as a scientist working overseas, but abroad is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a butterfly, and a lepidopterist is a scientist of butterflies and moths.

clue.text: Approve? As if!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be in favour of something
second meaning: a conjunction, as in 'it looks as if it will rain'

explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation dresses it up as a sarcastic exchange, but each part is a separate meaning of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb of approval and an informal conjunction standing in for 'as though'.

clue.text: Greek hero in epic poem abridged by American

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, so the poem's title loses its last letter

parts.note: Homer's epic poem
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American has made a cut-down version of a famous Greek epic.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is Homer's account of the hero's ten-year voyage home from Troy, so the definition and wordplay share a source.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus, Ulysses to the Romans, is the Greek hero whose voyage home is told in Homer's epic.

clue.text: Stop what you're doing and see what the strippers might do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: abandon all current tasks at once
second meaning, taken literally: let every item of clothing fall

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to look at a striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for abandoning your work is read literally as clothes falling to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for urgently abandoning all tasks, and literally describes letting every garment fall.

clue.text: Plant in photograph held up by monster

indicators.note: in a down entry, something held up by another sits on top of it

parts.note: a snap is a casual photograph
a dragon is a mythical monster

explanation.surface: A photo of a plant being carried aloft by a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden flower whose blooms open like a mouth.

clue.text: Wrote a novel dismissing Welsh goddess

indicators.note: novel means new, so the remaining letters take a new order
dismissing sends something away, so that letter is removed from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: Someone wrote a novel that leaves out the Welsh goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrote a novel' reads as authorship, but novel is the rearranging signal after W is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, minor goddesses of the arts, presiding over lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Prominent headline cut to accommodate paper's leader

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the cut wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a slash is a cut

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of paper

explanation.surface: An editor trims a big headline to make room for the lead story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' sounds like a newspaper's editorial, but here it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a splash is the main front-page story with its large headline.

clue.text: Ordinary sort of pudding

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the baked dessert of buttered bread slices in custard

explanation.walkthrough: Bread and butter pudding is a classic British baked dessert of buttered bread in egg custard.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adjective for basic everyday matters and the descriptor for a well-known baked dessert.

clue.text: Fantastic Sam Cooke record, originally a dollar

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wild, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of record

explanation.surface: A great Sam Cooke record that first cost just a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: Fantastic reads as praise for the soul singer's record, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Smackeroo is American slang for a dollar, a jokey variant of smacker.

clue.text: Benefit from a disguise, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or passed on by word of mouth, so we go by the sound

parts.note: a veil can serve as a disguise

explanation.surface: Someone profits from going about in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or advantage, as in 'to no avail', so it means benefit.

clue.text: Outer garment, article acquired on the way back

indicators.note: going on the way back is travelling in the opposite direction, so the pieces read right to left

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
got means obtained or acquired

explanation.surface: Picking up a coat or similar item during the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Passed over specially designed taps

indicators.note: something specially designed is made to a new pattern, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bespoke plumbing fittings that have been overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps looks like a plumbing noun; it is the verb for listening in on a phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a phone is to listen secretly, which is exactly what someone who eavesdrops does.

clue.text: Winger in Real Madrid ground?

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wide player in the Real Madrid stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Winger and ground suggest football, but the winger is a creature with wings and ground means crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral is a common butterfly, so a creature with wings.

clue.text: Open and shut, perhaps, according to how things turn out?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: how a box or suitcase may be, open or shut

definitions.text: according to how things turn out
definitions.meaning: second meaning: depending on the circumstances

explanation.walkthrough: 'Open and shut' sounds like a legal case that is easy to decide; read literally it is the states a container may be in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock idiom for 'depending on circumstances', and literally says what a container might be.

clue.text: Area of interest, one in Indonesian island fishing port

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the name of the island

parts.note: Bali is an island of Indonesia
Roman numeral one
Wick is a fishing town on the far north-east coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: Somebody's speciality turns out to be a harbour town on an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishing port is the small Scottish town in Caithness, not anywhere in Indonesia as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiwick was a bailiff's jurisdiction and now means a person's own field or sphere.

clue.text: Check on what sounds like expensive animal

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

indicators.note: what sounds like asks for a word with the same pronunciation but a different spelling

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: Checking on something that seems to be a costly beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer, or caribou, is a large Arctic animal of the deer family.

clue.text: An air hostess, say, could be like a social climber

parts.words: An air hostess, say, could be
parts.note: surface reading: flight attendants as people with social ambitions

parts.words: An air hostess, say, could be
parts.note: setter's reading: a flight attendant literally moves up into the sky at work

explanation.surface: Flight attendants are said to have their eyes on a higher social class.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase about rising in society is read literally of someone whose job carries them into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes people rising in social class, the aim of a social climber.

clue.text: Extremely drunk bishop on top of house?

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top of puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
house, or housey-housey, is the old British name for bingo, also called lotto

explanation.surface: A very drunk bishop who has climbed onto the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: House is not a building here but the British name for bingo, a numbers game also known as lotto.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for very drunk, in the same family as plastered or legless.

clue.text: Braggarts, noisy in front of traps

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece ahead of the second in the build

parts.note: loud means noisy
trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

explanation.surface: Boasters making a racket in front of some snares.
explanation.walkthrough: Traps looks like snares; it is slang for mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudmouth talks too much and boastfully, so braggarts fit as a near synonym.

clue.text: Strongly recommended drug? E? Unlikely

indicators.note: unlikely suggests something improbable or odd, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Was ecstasy, a drug, really what was recommended? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: E looks like slang for the drug ecstasy, but it is simply a letter in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to press or advise them strongly to act.

clue.text: British RU cap, one showing unusual courage?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a player capped by the British and Irish ... rugby union touring team
second meaning: a person who is very brave

explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union; a cap is a selection for a representative side, here the British and Irish Lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A player picked for the Lions is called a Lion, and a lion is the emblem of bravery.

clue.text: Undergarment in Dave's tallboy

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters running across the apostrophe and word break

explanation.surface: A singlet stored in a man's tall chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: A tallboy is a tall chest of drawers, just where a vest might be kept.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt worn under other clothes.

clue.text: Row involving good, formidable competitor

indicators.note: involving means taking in or including, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An argument involving a decent and tough opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel but means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger is used figuratively for a fierce, aggressive rival, as in an economic tiger.

clue.text: A variety of Argentine fruit

indicators.note: a variety of suggests a different form, so the letters take another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of fruit grown in Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: The tangerine is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, a type of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Flag used for a long time, covered in blood, left inside

parts.note: something old has been in use a long time

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the word for bloody

parts.note: gory means bloodstained
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A battered old banner, stained with blood, left indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is the nickname for the flag of the United States.

clue.text: Author, one adding fuel to the fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Bram ..., the Irish writer of Dracula

definitions.text: one adding fuel to the fire
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a person who tends a furnace or boiler

explanation.walkthrough: 'Adding fuel to the fire' suggests making trouble worse, but it is meant literally of a furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker shovels coal into a furnace, and Bram Stoker is the novelist behind Dracula.
